ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā and the following Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ form a pair assuring the Prophet of success; the former reflects intense Makkan opposition, the latter emerging signs of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.claim: Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ completes the preceding sūrah: 93:6’s sheltering and other favours concerned the period before and just after prophethood, while this sūrah points to blessings after Islam spread in Arabia.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.anchor: It begins after Sūrah al-Ḍuḥā without any prior introduction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.claim: The prior sūrah predicts a bright future; this one points to predictions already beginning to materialize and assures the Prophet that hardship yields to success if faced courageously.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.anchor: by making a reference to some such predictions which by then had shown clear signs to materialize, an emphatic assurance is sounded to the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.claim: The discourse proceeds from inner expansion, through the recurring law of hardship with relief, to completion of the mission and disciplined use of its success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.anchor: Initially a reference is made to the gift of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p364/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p364/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p364/r1.claim: This sūrah completes the reassurance begun in 93: its central lesson is the divine law that every hardship faced by an inviter to virtue is followed by relief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p364/r1.anchor: the law is in fact the real subject of the sūrah and is stated near its end in verses five and six

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r1.claim: The burden was the Prophet’s perplexity in seeking truth before prophethood and, later, the opposition of his people; his unanswered efforts and delayed revelation multiplied his worry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r2.claim: The Prophet feared his preaching might be inadequate because people evaded it despite greater effort; Sūrah Ṭāhā similarly reassures that revelation was not meant to distress him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r4.claim: The burden-removal sentence is coordinated with verse 1; its interrogative particle governs verse 2 as well, a construction Islahi also finds in Sūrah al-Naba.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p365/r4.anchor: co-ordinated in meaning with the first

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r7.claim: The burden removed from the Prophet is his sin before prophethood.

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r8.claim: Alternatively, God protected the Prophet from committing sin, removing a burden he had never incurred.
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r8.anchor: عصمناك عن ارتكاب الوزر ؛ فوضعه عنه بأنه لم يستوجبه قط

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r9.claim: Alternatively, God lightened the burdens of prophethood and made the Prophet carried by divine aid rather than bearing them alone.
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r9.anchor: خفضنا عنك أعباء النبوة وجعلناك محمولا لا متحملا

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r10.claim: God strengthened the Prophet to endure people and witness Him, preserved his trust, and guarded him from attending to people amid his honor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r10.anchor: قويناك لمشاهدتنا ، وحفظنا عليك ما استحفظت

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r11.claim: The burden weighed down the Prophet's back so heavily that without God's carrying it for him, it would have broken him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.claim: Lifting the burden is a metaphor for protection from sin and purification from defilement, expressed hyperbolically as if a burden had been removed from someone who had none.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p500/r2.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس، عبر عن ذلك بالحط

FARRA:v3p275#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p275#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p275#2/r2.claim: The removed burden is the sin of the pre-Islamic period; ʿAbd Allāh's reading says “we removed your burden.”
FARRA:v3p275#2/r2.anchor: «ووضعنا عنك وزرك» (2) ، يقول: إثم الجاهلية، وهي في قراءة عبد الله: «وحللنا عنك وقرك » ،

MAJAZ:v2p303/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p303/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p303/r1.claim: Wizrak means your sin or burden of sin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.claim: Some interpret the removed burden as the Prophet's pre-revelation weight of seeing Quraysh's idolatry without clear divine instruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.anchor: هو عند بعض المتأولين الثقل الذي كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وحيرته قبل المبعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and others say God lightened the burdens of prophethood and helped the Prophet bear people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وغيره المعنى: خففنا عليك أثقال النبوة وأعناك على الناس،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r7.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد والحسن وجمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r7.claim: Qatada, Ibn Zayd, al-Hasan, and most commentators identify the burden as sins, metaphorically called weight, and link the passage to 48:2.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن زيد والحسن وجمهور من المفسرين: الوزر هنا، الذنوب.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak, in al-Naqqash's book, includes attending gatherings with the Prophet's people that God disliked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: وفي كتاب النقاش حضوره مع قومه المشاهد التي لا يحبها الله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya groups such experiences with upbringing and says the Prophet's heart leaned toward right guidance; he never worshipped idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r9.anchor: وفي ذلك كله منيب إلى الصواب، وأما عبادة الأصنام فلم يلتبس بها قط،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r10.speaker: أنس بن مالك وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r10.claim: Anas reads wa-hatatna; Ibn Masud's and Ubayy's codices have variants with halala or hatatna, and Abu Amr says the Prophet approved them all.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p496#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك «وحططنا عنك وزرك» ،

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r6.claim: Wizr means a burden; a minister carries the ruler's burden, and sins are called burdens because they weigh on their bearer.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r6.anchor: والوزر: من الثقل، ومنه: الوزير لأنه يحمل الثقل عن الملك

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r14.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وابن زيد وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r14.claim: They interpret the burden removed from the Prophet as his sin.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r14.anchor: قيل: ذنبك، عن مجاهد، والضحاك، وابن زيد، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r15.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r15.claim: He interprets the burden as what the Prophet bore during the pre-prophetic period of ignorance.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r15.anchor: وقيل: الوزر الذي كان عليه في الجاهلية قبل النبوة، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r16.claim: He explains the burden as the Prophet's distress over opponents' abuse, removed when God gave him victory; the author calls this the best view.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r16.anchor: عن أبي مسلم. وهذا أحسن ما قيل فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r7.claim: Mujahid interprets the removed burden as forgiveness of the Prophet's sin; Qatada says his sins had weighed on him and God forgave them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r7.anchor: أحدها : وغفرنا لك ذنبك , قاله مجاهد , وقال قتادة : كان للنبي ذنوب أثقلته فغفرها الله تعالى له .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r8.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says God lifted the Prophet's load, as reflected in Ibn Masud's reading وحللنا عنك وقرك.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r8.anchor: الثاني : وحططنا عنك ثقلك , قاله السدي . وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود , وحللنا عنك وقرك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation says the Prophet was kept free of impurities during the forty years before revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r9.anchor: وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس حتى نزل عليك الوحي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r10.claim: Mawardi also says God dropped obligations the Prophet could not bear; prophets receive strength for the weight of their mission, so what others could not endure was bearable for them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p296#2/r10.anchor: أي أسقطنا عنك تكليف ما لم تطقه , لأن الأنبياء وإن حملوا من أثقال النبوة

ZAJJAJ:v5p341/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p341/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p341/r2.claim: Laying aside the burden means God forgave the Prophet’s earlier and later sins.
ZAJJAJ:v5p341/r2.anchor: أي وضعنا عنك إثمك أن غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Sharḥ Makkan and place it just after Sūrah 93; Ibn ʿAbbās calls it Madinan, while some assign only vv. 5–6 to Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.anchor: considered by most commentators to be a Makkan sūrah, most likely revealed immediately after the preceding one. Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that it is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.claim: Some say Sūrahs 93 and 94 were originally one, since Companions recited them together in one prayer cycle without a basmalah separating them.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.anchor: the Companions of the Prophet would recite them together in a single prayer cycle

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.claim: Ash-Sharh was revealed almost immediately after Ad-Duha and appears to continue it directly.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.anchor: revealed almost immediately af ter the preceding one, appears to be a direct continuation of the latter

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.speaker: Ta'us ibn Kaysan and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.claim: They regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah and recited them in prayer without a second basmala; Asad cites Razi.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.anchor: Ta'us ibn Kaysan, or the Caliph Umar i bn Abd al-Aziz (known as "the Second Umar") - regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.claim: The surah addresses the Prophet first and, through him, every true follower of the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.anchor: addressed in the first instance to the Prophet and, through him, to every true follower of the Qur'an

TABATABAI:94:1-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r8.claim: A burden is a heavy load; “making the back creak” evokes pressure so great it produces an audible sound, hence the burden's palpable weight.
TABATABAI:94:1-5/r8.anchor: الوزر الحمل الثقيل، وإنقاض الظهر كسره بحيث يسمع له صوت

TABATABAI:94:2-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r1.claim: Lifting the burden removes its felt weight; the phrase is coordinated with “did We not expand your chest,” which implicitly means “We have expanded it.”
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r1.anchor: ووضع الوزر إذهاب ما يحس من ثقله

TABATABAI:94:2-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r2.claim: In context, lifting the Prophet's burden means making his mission succeed by arranging the means for his struggle; the message and its call are the load he carried after his chest was expanded.
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r2.anchor: إنفاذ دعوته وإمضاء مجاهدته في الله بتوفيق الأسباب

TABATABAI:94:2-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r3.claim: Reported explanations include the chest-splitting tradition, pre-prophetic acts, lack of knowledge of revealed law, uncertainty about fulfilling the mission, and the early weight of revelation.
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r3.anchor: وقيل وضع الوزر إشارة إلى ما وردت به الرواية أن ملكين نزلا عليه وفلقا صدره

TABATABAI:94:2-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r4.claim: Other proposed burdens are distress at people's misguidance, their persecution, grief over Abu Talib and Khadija, sin removed by infallibility, or the community's sin forgiven for him; the author calls some foolish, others weak and out of context.
TABATABAI:94:2-5/r4.anchor: وهذه الوجوه بعضها سخيف وبعضها ضعيف لا يلائم السياق

THALABI:v10p232#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p232#3/r2.claim: The burden that weighed on the Prophet’s back was lifted and had weakened him; an exhausted camel worn down by travel is also called naqḍ.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r2.anchor: وحططنا عنك وزرك الذي أنقض ظهرك أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه

THALABI:v10p232#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p232#3/r3.claim: He explains the burden as breaking the Prophet’s back when he heard its naqiḍ, meaning its sound.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: كسر ظهرك حين سمع نقيضه

THALABI:v10p232#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
THALABI:v10p232#3/r4.claim: They identify the burden with what the Prophet had done before Islam.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r4.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة والضحاك: يعني ما سلف منه في الجاهلية

THALABI:v10p232#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v10p232#3/r5.claim: He interprets the burden as error and inadvertence.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r5.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني الخطأ والسهو

THALABI:v10p232#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p232#3/r6.claim: The burden means the community’s sins, attributed to the Prophet because his heart was occupied and concerned with them.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r6.anchor: ذنوب أمتك فأضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها واهتمامه لها

THALABI:v10p232#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r7.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
THALABI:v10p232#3/r7.claim: They understand the burden as the duties of prophethood and its responsibilities, which God made lighter for him.
THALABI:v10p232#3/r7.anchor: يعني خففنا عليك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها

THALABI:v10p232#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p232#3/r8.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p232#3/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that God protected the Prophet from bearing sin.

BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r2.claim: Removing the burden means lifting its heavy load; placing عنك before the object hastens the good news and makes the reader anticipate it.
BURSEVI:v10p356#2/r2.anchor: أي حططنا وأسقطنا عنك حملك الثقيل وعنك متعلق بوضعنا وتقديمه على المفعول

QASHANI:94:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:94:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:94:1/r3.claim: The prophetic burden is carrying revelation and duties: in witnessing, the Prophet saw only God and could not distinguish acts or command and forbid; returning from sainthood to prophethood, the heart’s veil nearly broke his back. Empowerment in abiding lets him see unity in multiplicity without losing witness during the call, removing the burden and raising his mention.
QASHANI:94:1/r3.anchor: ثقل ذلك عليه وكاد أن يقصم ظهره لاحتجابه عن الشهود الذاتي

SULAMI:v2p404/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p404/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p404/r3.claim: The burden removed was the load of prophethood and messengership: the Prophet was carried through it rather than bearing it alone.
SULAMI:v2p404/r3.anchor: وقال في قوله : ﴿ ووضعنا عنك وزرك ﴾ [ الآية : 2 ] : أعباء النبوة والرسالة

SULAMI:v2p404/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p404/r4.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p404/r4.claim: God enabled the Prophet to endure opponents and strengthened him to proclaim the message when the burden nearly exhausted him.
SULAMI:v2p404/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : ﴿ ووضعنا عنك وزرك ﴾ ألم نمن عليك بالاحتمال من المخالفين

SULAMI:v2p404/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p404/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p404/r7.claim: Removing the burden means removing awareness of creatures from the Prophet's inner secret.
SULAMI:v2p404/r7.anchor: وقال في قوله : ﴿ ووضعنا عنك وزرك ﴾ ألم أزل ملاحظة المخلوقين عن سرك

SULAMI:v2p404/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p404/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p404/r8.claim: God lightened the burden by preserving the Prophet in what he was entrusted with and protecting him.
SULAMI:v2p404/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم خففنا عنك بحفظ ما استحفظت وحفظنا عنك

SULAMI:v2p404/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p404/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p404/r9.claim: God protected the Prophet from impurity through his first forty years until prophethood and revelation appeared.
SULAMI:v2p404/r9.anchor: وقال في قوله : ﴿ ووضعنا عنك وزرك ﴾ قال : حفظتك في الأربعين من الأدناس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts God's answer to his request for prophetic miracles: God reminded him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, enrichment, opening his chest, removing his burden, and raising his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.claim: The Prophet says that after he asked about miracles granted earlier prophets, God reminded him He had sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, opened his chest, and raised his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the burden is Muhammad's sin, which weighed heavily on him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ووضعنا عنك وزرك قال : ذنبك الذي انقض ظهرك قال : اثقل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r2.speaker: شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r2.claim: Shurayh ibn Ubayd says God forgave Muhammad's sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r2.anchor: عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي ووضعنا عنك وزرك قال : وغفرنا لك ذنبك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.claim: Mujahid notes that Abdullah's reading has 'we relieved you of your burden.'
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : في قراءة عبد الله ' وحللنا عنك وقرك '

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.claim: A report says God answered Muhammad's comparison with Abraham and Moses by recalling his own blessings, including raised remembrance, and saying that He had chosen him as a close friend.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة اني لم اكن سالته

TUSTARI:94:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:94:2/r1.claim: God removed the natural self's attachment to other than Him, making the Prophet rest in God and receptive through Him.
TUSTARI:94:2/r1.anchor: يعني أزلنا عنك السكون إلى غيرنا من همة نفس الطبع، فجعلناك ساكنا إلينا قابلا عنا بنا.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.claim: The burden was removed in part by guidance to truth, which ended the Prophet's distress over his people, and by provision for a livelihood that could distract him from reflection on reform.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p412/r1.anchor: وأما وضع الوزر عنه فحاصل بأمرين : بهدايته إلى الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك والفراء وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r1.claim: They interpret laying down the burden as removing the Prophet's earlier sins from the pre-Islamic period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r1.anchor: أي حططنا عنك إثمك الذي سلف في الجاهلية قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands this as forgiveness for the Prophet's earlier and later sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى أنه غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r3.claim: The root sense of burden is something a person carries on his back, used here as a metaphor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p162#3/r3.anchor: وأصل الوزر ما حمله الإنسان على ظهره فشبه بالحمل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r1.claim: Removing Muhammad's burden is like God's promise to forgive his earlier and later sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r1.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك} بمعنى: {ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر} [الفتح: 2]

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r1.claim: One answer is that even minor prophetic sins caused acute grief, regret, and sorrow.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r1.anchor: لشدة اغتمامهم بها، وتحسرهم على وقوعها مع ندم عليها،

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r2.claim: Another view says the question does not arise under Abū Muslim's interpretation of the burden.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r2.anchor: وعلى ما أوله أبو مسلم لا سؤال عليه

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r3.claim: Some say a prophet's greater standing and greater blessings make his sin more serious; another says the matter itself was grave.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r3.anchor: وقيل: لأن محلهم عند الله أعظم، ونعمه أكثر، فكان ذنبهم أعظم، وقيل: لأن الأمر أعظم،

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r4.claim: The burden may mean the community's sins, attributed to the Prophet because he is deeply concerned about them.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد به ذنوب أمته، فأضافه إليه لاهتمامه به،

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r5.claim: Other interpretations take the burden as an inadvertent lapse or mistake.

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads the burden as the heavy duties of prophethood and carrying out its mission, which God eased.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r6.anchor: وقيل: (ووضعنا عنك وزرك) يعني: خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها،

JISHUMI:v10p7465/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r7.claim: Another view understands the phrase as God's protection from sin, called removal because without protection the burden would break the Prophet's back.
JISHUMI:v10p7465/r7.anchor: وقيل: عصمناك عن الوزر، فسمى عصمته وضعا أي: لولا العصمة لأنقض ظهرك.

KASHSHAF:94:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:94:2/r1.claim: Lifting the burden can mean forgiving him, teaching him the laws, or clearing his case after he proclaimed the message and it reached others.
KASHSHAF:94:2/r1.anchor: ووضعه عنه : أن غفر له ،   أو علم الشرائع

KASHSHAF:94:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:2/r2.speaker: أنس
KASHSHAF:94:2/r2.claim: Anas reads the verb as halallna, meaning We unburdened or released.

KASHSHAF:94:2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:94:2/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads, We unburdened you of your burden.

KASHSHAF:94:4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:94:4/r2.claim: The added laka creates a suspenseful allusion then clarification: first what was expanded is left implicit before the breast is named, and similarly with your mention and burden.
KASHSHAF:94:4/r2.anchor: في زيادة لك ما في طريقة الإبهام والإيضاح ،   كأنه قيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r4.claim: The burden that made the Prophet's back creak may represent pre-prophethood lapses, ignorance of rulings, or grief over his people's obstinacy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r4.anchor: والوزر الذي أنقض ظهره أي : حمله على النقيض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r5.claim: Removing the burden may mean forgiveness, teaching religious law, or establishing his excuse after he delivered the message.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r5.anchor: ووضعه عنه : أن غفر له ، أو علم الشرائع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r6.speaker: أنس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r6.claim: Anas reads the phrase as “and We unburdened” or released.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud reads “and We unburdened your load.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p775#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( وحللنا عنك وقرك )

MUJAHID:v2p767/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p767/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p767/r1.claim: Mujahid says the burden removed was the Prophet’s sin in the pre-Islamic period.
MUJAHID:v2p767/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ووضعنا عنك وزرك ﴾ قال ذنبك في الجاهلية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#2/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God lightened the burdens of prophethood; another says the burden was an unspecified lapse, leaving the preferable action while doing the good, for which prophets are reproached and forgiven.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p346#2/r1.anchor: وخففنا عنك اعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها وقيل هو زلة لا تعرف بعينها وهى ترك الأفضل

NAHHAS:v5p251/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p251/r9.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p251/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses wizr as the Prophet's sin in the pre-Islamic period; the verb is wazara and the passive participle mawzūr.
NAHHAS:v5p251/r9.anchor: قال الحسن وزره ذنبه في الجاهلية يقال وزر يزر وزرا والمفعول موزور

NAHHAS:v5p251/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p251/r10.speaker: النبي
NAHHAS:v5p251/r10.claim: A report has the Prophet say, 'Return burdened, not rewarded'; some hadith scholars instead say maʾzūrāt, which, if sound, is a phonetic following form.
NAHHAS:v5p251/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث ارجعن موزورات غير مأجورات ومن أهل الحديث من يقول مأزورات

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r1.claim: Removing the burden means taking away the Prophet's sin; Anas's reading is wa-hallalna wa-hatatna, while Ibn Masud reads wa-hallalna anka wiqrak.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r1.anchor: أي حططنا عنك ذنبك. وقرأ أنس «وحللنا، وحططنا».

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r2.claim: This verse parallels the promise to forgive the Prophet's earlier and later sins; some say all the sins concerned preceded prophethood.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r3.claim: Qatada, Hasan, and al-Dahhak say the Prophet had sins weighing on him that God forgave.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة والحسن والضحاك: كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب أثقلته فغفرها الله له.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r4.claim: The burden refers to what weighed down the Prophet from his people's pre-Islamic ways, although he never worshipped an idol or image.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3/r4.anchor: ما كنت فيه من أمر الجاهلية لأنه كان صلى الله عليه وسلم في كثير من مذاهب قومه

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.claim: Bawani al-zawr means the foundations of the chest, and burden means a heavy load; al-Muhasibi says it would have remained weighty had God not pardoned it.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r1.anchor: «بواني زوره»: أي أصول صدره. فالوزر: الحمل الثقيل. قال المحاسبي:

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.claim: Al-Muhasibi explains why forgiven prophetic sins are described as heavy: prophets are deeply concerned, regretful, and sorrowful about them.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r2.anchor: قال: وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء بهذا الثقل، مع كونها مغفورة، لشدة اهتمامهم بها،

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi interprets removing the burden as lifting the Prophet's weight; the reading attributed to Abd Allah ibn Masud says the same with wiqrak.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: «ووضعنا عنك وزرك» أي وحططنا عنك ثقلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r4.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the burden refers to slips and inadvertent errors.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r4.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني الخطأ والسهو.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r5.claim: Another view takes the burden as the sins of the Prophet's community, attributed to him because his heart was occupied with their plight.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ذنوب أمتك، أضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r6.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r6.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Abu Ubayda interpret the burden as the duties of prophethood, which God made lighter.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r6.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة: خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r7.claim: Another report says revelation initially weighed so heavily that the Prophet nearly cast himself from a mountain until Gabriel appeared and relieved his fear of losing his reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r7.anchor: وقيل كان في الابتداء يثقل عليه الوحي، حتى كاد يرمي نفسه من شاهق الجبل،

QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r8.claim: A further interpretation is that God protected the Prophet from bearing sin and kept him pure from impurity throughout the forty years before revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:2-3#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: عصمناك عن احتمال الوزر، وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس

QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r1.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:2/r2.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet's back almost to breaking; God removed it by opening his heart, making the task lighter and easier.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r1.anchor: عبئك الذي أثقل ظهرك حتى كاد يحطمه من ثقله

QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.claim: God eased the burden by enabling the mission, opening hearts to it, and sending revelation that disclosed truth and helped convey it gently to people.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:3/r2.anchor: وبتوفيقك وتيسيرك للدعوة ومداخل القلوب . وبالوحي الذي يكشف لك عن الحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.claim: The chest is named because Satan's whispering occurs there; expansion removes whispering and replaces it with good impulses.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r1.anchor: لأن محل الوسوسة هو الصدر على ما قال : { يوسوس فى صدور الناس }

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.claim: The heart is the seat of reason and knowledge, guarded by the chest; if Satan enters the chest he brings worry, grief, and greed, constricting the heart and spoiling worship, while early resistance restores ease.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي الترمذي : القلب محل العقل والمعرفة ، وهو الذي يقصده الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.claim: The phrase 'for you' may indicate reciprocity: the Prophet performs all worship for God, and God performs His acts for the Prophet; alternatively, the mission's benefit returns to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r3.anchor: وثانيها : أن فيها تنبيها على أن منافع الرسالة عائدة إليه عليه السلام ، كأنه تعالى قال : إنما شرحنا صدرك لأجلك لا لأجلي

RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.claim: Using 'We' either magnifies the gift beyond comprehension or includes God's angels, whose presence strengthened the Prophet and made his opponents afraid.
RAZI-FULL:v32p4/r4.anchor: إن حملناه على نون التعظيم ، فالمعنى أن عظمة المنعم تدل على عظمة النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r1.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the conjunction follows the meaning of 'Did We not expand?'—'We expanded'—rather than its surface form; otherwise it should read 'and We place.'
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r1.anchor: قال المبرد : هذا محمول على معنى ألم نشرح لا على لفظه ، لأنك لا تقول ألم وضعنا

RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r2.claim: Wizr is the weight of sin, as in the verse about carrying burdens, and is compared to God's forgiveness of the Prophet's earlier and later sin.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5/r2.anchor: معنى الوزر ثقل الذنب ، وقد مر تفسيره عند قوله : { وهم يحملون أوزارهم }

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r1.claim: Those who allow minor sins for prophets take the burden as one of these, despite its severity, because the Prophet deeply regretted it and its effect on reward was serious though forgiven.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r1.anchor: الذين يجوزون الصغائر على الأنبياء عليهم السلام حملوا هذه الآية عليها

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r2.claim: Al-Qadi objects that if forgiveness of a minor sin is obligatory, it cannot be a favor for which God takes credit.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r2.anchor: وهو أن العفو عن الصغيرة واجب على الله تعالى عند القاضي ، والله تعالى ذكر هذه الآية في معرض الامتنان

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the burden was sins committed before prophethood, which God forgave.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : قال قتادة : كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب سلفت منه في الجاهلية قبل النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r4.claim: It may instead be the heavy duties of prophecy, which God made easy to carry and fulfill.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r4.anchor: أن المراد منه تخفيف أعباء النبوة التي تثقل الظهر من القيام بأمرها

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r5.claim: Another proposal is distress at the changes people made to Abraham's religion, which Muhammad could not stop until God strengthened him and commanded him to follow Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : الوزر ما كان يكرهه من تغييرهم لسنة الخليل . وكان لا يقدر على منعهم إلى أن قواه الله

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r6.claim: The sins of the Prophet's community may have weighed on him; God reassured him against their immediate punishment and promised his intercession in the hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أنها ذنوب أمته صارت كالوزر عليه ، ماذا يصنع في حقهم إلى أن قال : { وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم }

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r7.claim: The 'burden' may be a figurative removal of a sin that would have crushed him: before prophethood God once made him sleep through a wedding with music.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r7.anchor: وخامسها : معناه عصمناك عن الوزر الذي ينقض ظهرك ، لو كان ذلك الذنب حاصلا ، فسمى العصمة وضعا مجازا

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r8.claim: It may have been the terror of first meeting Gabriel: Muhammad shook and nearly threw himself from a mountain, then grew familiar with him and longed to see him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r8.anchor: وسادسها : الوزر ما أصابه من الهيبة والفزع في أول ملاقاة جبريل عليه السلام ، حين أخذته الرعدة

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r9.claim: It may be the abuse and insults that first shook him and nearly crushed his back; later he endured even bloodied attacks while praying for his people.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r9.anchor: ما كان يلحقه من الأذى والشتم حتى كاد ينقض ظهره وتأخذه الرعدة

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r10.claim: If the surah followed the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadija, their loss was a great burden; God lifted it by taking him heavenward, where angels greeted him and his renown rose.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r10.anchor: وثامنها : لئن كان نزول السورة بعد موت أبي طالب وخديجة ، فلقد كان فراقهما عليه وزرا عظيما

RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r11.claim: The burden may be pre-prophetic perplexity about how to serve God amid unceasing blessings; revelation clarified how he should worship, easing the shame of inadequate service.
RAZI-FULL:v32p5#2/r11.anchor: وتاسعها : أن المراد من الوزر والثقل الحيرة التي كانت له قبل البعثة ، وذلك أنه بكمال عقله

STUDYQURAN:94:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:2/r1.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:94:2/r1.claim: Many commentators take lifting the burden as an allusion to the Prophet being forgiven all his sins.
STUDYQURAN:94:2/r1.anchor: This verse is seen by many commentators as an allusion to the Prophet’s being forgiven all sins

TAB:94:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r3.speaker: author
TAB:94:1/r3.claim: Putting down the burden means forgiving past sins and removing the weight of the days of ignorance before Islam.
TAB:94:1/r3.anchor: وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك ،   وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية التي كنت فيها

TAB:94:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB:94:1/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah has ‘we released your load’ in place of ‘we removed your burden.’
TAB:94:1/r4.anchor: في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر :  «وَحَلَلْنا عَنْكَ وِقْرَكَ »

TAB:94:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:1/r6.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had sins that weighed him down, and God forgave them.
TAB:94:1/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ

TAB:94:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:94:1/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the burden as the associating of partners with God in which Muhammad had been involved.
TAB:94:1/r7.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول ،   في قوله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ يعني :  الشرك الذي كان فيه

TAB:94:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:1/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:1/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says God expanded Muhammad's chest and forgave the sin he had before being commissioned as a prophet.
TAB:94:1/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  شرح له صدرَه

TAB:94:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:3/r2.claim: Qatada says Muhammad had sins that weighed him down and that God forgave them.
TAB:94:3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ

TAB:94:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:3/r3.claim: A second transmission from Qatada repeats that the Prophet's burdensome sins were forgiven by God.
TAB:94:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ قال :  كانت للنبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

TAB:94:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:94:3/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the burden God removed was the shirk in which Muhammad had been involved.
TAB:94:3/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول ،   في قوله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ يعني :  الشرك الذي كان فيه

TAB:94:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God expanded Muhammad's chest and forgave his sin from before prophethood.
TAB:94:3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  شرح له صدرَه

TAB:94:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:3/r7.speaker: author
TAB:94:3/r7.claim: The removed burden is described as Muhammad's sin that weighed down his back; God lifted it and made the load lighter.
TAB:94:3/r7.anchor: قال :  ذنبك الذي أنقض ظهرك :  أثقل ظهرَك ،   ووضعناه عنك ،   وخفّفنا عنك ما أثقل ظهرَك

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r1.claim: God removed Muḥammad's former sins and the weight of his pre-Islamic life; the burden had weighed down and weakened his back.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} [الشرح: 2] قال: ذنبك

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r2.claim: The phrase describes a heavy travel-worn camel whose journey has weakened it and removed its flesh.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r2.anchor: وأذهب لحمه: هو نقض سفر، وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the burden is Muḥammad's sin and the phrase says it weighed on his back.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} [الشرح: 2] قال: ذنبك وقوله: {الذي أنقض ظهرك} [الشرح: 3] قال: أثقل ظهرك

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r4.claim: Qatāda says sins had burdened the Prophet, and God forgave them.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ألم نشرح لك صدرك ووضعنا عنك وزرك الذي أنقض ظهرك} [الشرح: 2] كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the burden as the polytheism Muḥammad had been involved in.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله: {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} [الشرح: 2] يعني: الشرك الذي كان فيه

TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God forgave the sin from before Muḥammad's commissioning and compares its weight to a heavy camel load.
TAB-FULL:v24p492#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ألم نشرح لك صدرك ووضعنا عنك وزرك} [الشرح: 2] قال: شرح له صدره، وغفر له ذنبه الذي كان قبل أن ينبأ

TABRISI:94:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:94:1/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:94:1/r2.claim: Wizr means a burden; vizier derives from bearing the ruler's burdens, and sins are called burdens for their great punishment.
TABRISI:94:1/r2.anchor: الوزر الثقل في اللغة ومنه اشتق اسم الوزير لتحمله أثقال الملك

TABRISI:94:2-3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:94:2-3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:94:2-3/r2.claim: The confirming question means God had in fact expanded the Prophet's chest, as the coordinated statement that He removed his burden confirms.
TABRISI:94:2-3/r2.anchor: ومعنى الاستفهام في الآية التقرير أي قد فعلنا ذلك ويدل عليه قوله في العطف عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r1.claim: “We removed” follows the meaning of the preceding rhetorical question, not its surface form; following the surface would require the present-tense “we remove.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r1.anchor: قال المبرد: هذا محمول على معنى "ألم نشرح" لاعلى لفظه، لأنك لا تقول: ألم وضعنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r2.claim: Wizr means the weight of sin; the phrase is discussed with the image of people carrying their burdens on their backs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r2.anchor: ومعنى الوزر: ثقل الذنب (¬1)، وقد مر تفسيره عند قوله: {وهم يحملون أوزارهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Muqātil say God lifted the Prophet's past sins from the pre-Islamic period, like 48:2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p123#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) في رواية الكلبي، (والحسن (¬4) (¬5)، وقتادة (¬6)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.claim: One interpretation says the sins occurred before prophethood, in the pre-Islamic period.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r6.anchor: هذا الذي ذكرنا في الآيتين على قول من يقول: كانت له ذنوب سلفت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.claim: Others identify the burden as minor sins, mistakes, or lapses; although forgiven, they distressed the Prophet because he regretted and grieved over them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r7.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن المراد بهذا: الصغائر، والخطأ، والسهو، وإنما وصف ذلك بإنقاض الظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that God eased the burdens of prophethood—its duties, preservation, and rights—by making them manageable; al-Kisāʾī and Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk are associated with this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p125#2/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكسائي (¬1)، وجويبر عن الضحاك

WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r1.claim: Laying aside the burden means lifting what preceded from Muhammad's pre-Islamic life.
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r1.anchor: حططنا { عنك وزرك } ما سلف منك في الجاهلية

WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r2.claim: One reported view says the burden was error and forgetfulness.

WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r3.claim: Another reported view says God eased the burdens of prophethood.
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r3.anchor: وقيل : معناه خففنا عليك أعباء النبوة

WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:94:2/r4.claim: In Arabic, a burden is a heavy load.

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r1.claim: Wada can mean to place, lower, or remove; here God unloads the burden, wholly or partly. Vizr is a heavy load and also means guilt.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r1.anchor: “Vaz‘” mutlak koymak mânasına olduğu gibi aşağılatmak, indirmek, ıskāt etmek mânalarına da gelir.

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.speaker: Bir kısım müfessirîn
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r8.claim: Some exegetes read vizr as heavy sin, citing 6:31, and interpret removing it as forgiveness like 48:2.

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.claim: Elmalılı rejects the sin reading as unlikely: vizr's weight and the emphatic back-crushing description do not suit minor lapses that can be attributed to prophets.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r9.anchor: Onun için bunun günah mânasına değil ağır yük, hıml-i sakīl, bâr-ı girân mânasıyla Peygamber’i nübüvvetten evvel

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.claim: He prefers burdensome difficulties before or at the beginning of prophethood, the majority's choice; an alternative says the Prophet's exceptional sensitivity made even a small lapse weigh heavily.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r10.anchor: olabilirse de hilâf-ı zâhir olmaktan kurtulmaz

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.claim: One proposed burden was the bewilderment of seeing pre-Islamic society's idolatry and ignorance, while recognizing God's blessings yet not knowing how to serve Him; revelation removed that distress.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r11.anchor: Nübüvvet gelince bu hayret zâil olmuş, onun muktezâsı olan vizir üzerinden atılmıştır

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.claim: Burden and sin converge as spiritual pain, but differ in outcome: hardship's pain can end in reward and pleasure, whereas sin's pleasure leads to later pain.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r12.anchor: Gönülde duyulan gam ve eleme “vizr” tâbir edilmesi bu itibar iledir. Ancak yük elemi zâil olarak sonu bir ecr ü hazza müntehî olmak

ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.claim: A generous person feels ashamed to enjoy gifts without serving their giver; when service is offered, even heavy work becomes welcome and light, as happened when prophethood gave the Prophet a path of service.
ELMALILI:94:2-3/r13.anchor: Kerîm, âlîcenab kimse ise gördüğü in‘âma karşı hizmet edememiş veya o nimeti yerine sarf eyleyememiş olmaktan sıkılır

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.claim: A second proposed burden was the grave responsibility and fear of properly receiving and carrying out the prophetic mission, and of failing before God and people.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r1.anchor: O da risâlet vazifesinin hakkıyla telakkī ve îfâsındaki azîm meşakkat ve mes’ûliyet endişesi

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.claim: As knowledge and recognition increase, fear of God grows, in keeping with 35:28.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r2.anchor: ilim ziyadeleşip marifet arttıkça haşyetullah da artıyor

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.claim: At his first meeting with Gabriel, the Prophet trembled under the awe of the powerful angel described in 53:5–6.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r3.anchor: Evvelâ Cibrîl’e ilk mülâkātında bütün cühd ü tâkatini saran

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.claim: After gradually adapting to revelation, he faced unbelievers' abuse and hostility before receiving the promise of protection in 5:67 or the glad tidings in 93:4–5.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r4.anchor: kâfirlerin o zamana kadar görülmeyen ezâ ve cefâ ve türlü dedikodularla husûmet ve adâvetlerini görmeye başlamıştı

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.claim: The temporary cessation of revelation, loneliness, and mockery also grieved him and added to his worldly and otherworldly anxieties.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r5.anchor: Bir müddet için dinlendirilmek üzere vahyin fetret ve inkıtâ‘ından dolayı duyduğu yalnızlık ve işittiği şemâtetten dolayı

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.claim: With continued revelation and al-Duha, God removed some burdens and lightened others through habituation and greater insight, giving the Prophet spiritual strength and making the world seem negligible.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r6.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak, vahyin tevâlîsi ve Ve’d-duhâ’nın inzâliyle bunların bir kısmını büsbütün üzerinden atmış, bir kısmını da alıştırmak

ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.claim: Through the Qur'an's blessing, God began to raise the Prophet's name, honor, and standing in this world and the Hereafter.
ELMALILI:94:2-3#2/r7.anchor: Kur’ân’ın feyziyle dünya ve âhiret nâm u şânını, zikir ve haysiyetini yükseltmeye başlamış idi

CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.claim: Psalmic imagery may underlie the phrase, especially Psalm 4:2’s image of God making room in distress; the opening also directly uses the divine ‘we’ as in 97:1 and 108:1.
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:1-3:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Wie auch in V. 2 und 4 könnte dabei eine psalmische Bildsprache im Hintergrund stehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:94:2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The image of relief from a burden on the back is also found in Psalm 81:7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Auch die Entlastung des Rückens ist ein psalmisches Motiv, s. Psalm 81:7

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.claim: The burden removed may be the Prophet's anguish at his society's faith and morals, quieted or eased when revelation gave him hope and relief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r5.anchor: arasında yaşadığı topluluğun inanç ve ahlâk yönünden içine düştüğü durumdan dolayı duyduğu ıstırabın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.claim: Alternatively, God removed the burden by granting support in establishing monotheism and virtues such as justice, honesty, mercy, and cooperation in good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:1/r6.anchor: Tevhid inancını ve insan ilişkilerinde adalet, dürüstlük, merhamet, iyilikte yardımlaşma gibi erdemleri hâkim kılma mücadelesinde

ALUSI-FULL:v30p165/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p165/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p165/r7.claim: A report about the Night Journey has God remind Muhammad that He sheltered, guided, enriched him, expanded his chest, removed his burden, and raised his mention, demonstrating the surahs' thematic connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p165/r7.anchor: يا محمد ألم أجدك يتيما فآويت وضالا فهديت وعائلا فأغنيت وشرحت لك صدرك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r1.claim: The clause coordinates with the implied sense of the previous one: God expanded the Prophet's chest and removed his burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r1.anchor: عطف على ما أشير إليه من مدلول الجملة السابقة كأنه قيل قد شرحنا لك صدرك ووضعنا الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r2.claim: عنْك is fronted before the direct object to hasten the joyful news and suspense; leaving the long object before it would disrupt the verse's balanced phrasing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r2.anchor: وتقديمه على المفعول الصريح لما مر من القصد إلى تعجيل المسرة والتشويق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r3.claim: وزر means a heavy load, so the phrase says God lifted the Prophet's heavy burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p168#2/r3.anchor: والوزر الحمل الثقيل أي وحططنا عنك حملك الثقيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.claim: The Prophet recounts asking about other prophets' gifts; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, provision, an opened breast, and removal of his burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وودت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r6.speaker: غيره عن حماد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r6.claim: A variant adds God's reminder that He opened the Prophet's breast and removed his burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r6.anchor: وزاد غيره عن حماد قال: ألم أشرح لك صدرك ووضعت عنك وزرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r2.claim: They interpret the removed burden as what had preceded from the Prophet in the pre-Islamic period, connecting it to 48:2.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن، ومجاهد وقتادة، والضحاك: وحططنا عنك الذي سلف منك في الجاهلية، وهو كقوله: "ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r3.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r3.claim: He interprets the burden as error and forgetfulness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني الخطأ والسهو

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r4.claim: Another view takes the burden as the sins of the Prophet's community, attributed to him because he was preoccupied with them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: ذنوب أمتك [فأضافه] (2) إليه لاشتغال قلبه بهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r5.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r5.claim: They understand the burden as the weight of prophethood and its responsibilities, which God lightened.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p463#2/r5.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة: يعني خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:1-3/r4.claim: The burden lifted from the Prophet is a heavy load.

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.claim: A report likens reciting this sura to visiting the Prophet while distressed and relieving him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة ألم نشرح فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتم ففرج عني

BINTSHATI:v1p62/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r2.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r2.claim: Some call the addressed prepositional phrases unnecessary additions, saying they clarify an initially vague object.
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r2.anchor: وقيل في {لِكِ} هنا، إنها زيادة يستقل المعنى بدونها!!

BINTSHATI:v1p62/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r3.claim: That proposed clarification would require stopping before لك, but readers unanimously connect the phrase; صدرَك already identifies what was opened, as the following objects do.
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r3.anchor: ولا نعلم أحداً من القراء قرأها بالوقف، بل الإجماع على قراءتها وصلاً

BINTSHATI:v1p62/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r4.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r4.claim: Al-Nishaburi describes لك as an insertion and lists possible functions such as generality followed by specification, exclusivity, or emphasis.
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r4.anchor: الإجمال ثم التفصيل، وإرادة الاختصاص، أو كونه أهم

BINTSHATI:v1p62/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r5.claim: The ordinary Arabic construction needs no extra theory: fronted prepositional phrases naturally strengthen emphasis, exclusive address, and connection.
BINTSHATI:v1p62/r5.anchor: وإنما للتقرير وتأكيد الاختصاص وتقوية الإيصال

BINTSHATI:v1p63/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r1.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r1.claim: Abduh says fronting لك, عنك, and لك before their objects adds emphasis and brings the good news quickly.

BINTSHATI:v1p63/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r2.claim: Ordinary Arabic expressions show that these pronouns are purposeful rather than redundant.
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r2.anchor: وإنما هي ضرورة بيانية اقتضاها المقام

BINTSHATI:v1p63/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r5.claim: Waḍʿ means lowering, casting down, or removing, and is often used for something heavy or burdensome, including childbirth.
BINTSHATI:v1p63/r5.anchor: الوضع الحطُّ والإلقاء والطرح زالإسقاط، وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يثقل ويرْهق

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.claim: In both literal and figurative Quranic uses, waḍʿ evokes relief from a heavy load: war's burdens, weapons, shackles, and the Prophet's burden.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r1.anchor: فشهد هذا التتبع الاستقرائي، على أن الوضع ملحوظ فيه دائماً، التخفف من ثقل مرهق وحمل باهظ

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.claim: Wizr first means a mountain and by extension a refuge; wazīr shares the load, and the term then denotes physical weight or moral sin.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r2.anchor: وأصل الوزر: الجبل، وسمى الملجأ وزراً

BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.claim: The paired image of removing the burden and the burden that made the back give way emphasizes how oppressive its weight had been.
BINTSHATI:v1p64/r3.anchor: والوضع للوزر في آية الشرح، يؤكد ثقل العبء، كما تؤكده الآية بعدها

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.claim: Al-Raghib reads the burden as the customs of pre-Islamic ignorance from which Muhammad was specially exempted.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r5.anchor: هو ما كنت فيه من إصر الجاهلية، وأعفيت منه بما خصصت به

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan interprets the burden figuratively as protection from sins and purification from defilement.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r6.anchor: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس

BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the burden as past sins forgiven and the weight of the Prophet's earlier days lifted.
BINTSHATI:v1p65/r7.anchor: وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك، وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.speaker: قتادة
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had sins that weighed on him, which God forgave.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r1.anchor: كانت للنبي ذنوب قد أثقلته فغفرها تعالى له

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the burden as shirk; the author corrects this to the shirk of Muhammad's people.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r2.anchor: والأولى عندنا أن يقال: الشرك الذي كان فيه قومه.

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.claim: Other interpretations include pre-prophetic minor sins, ignorance of revealed laws, intense concern to bring stubborn people to Islam, the burdens of the mission, or pre-revelation bewilderment.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r3.anchor: وقيل: ما أثقل ظهره لما صدر عنه من بعض الصغائر قبل النبوة

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.claim: Abduh reads the image as the crushing psychological burden of concern for his people and uncertainty before revelation, heavier than any physical load.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r4.anchor: ما كان يحمله عليه السلام من ثقل الاهتمام بشأن قومه، وضيق المذاهب بين يديه

BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.claim: The author agrees with Abduh: the burden is the pre-revelation confusion and failure to find the straight path described in 93:7.
BINTSHATI:v1p66/r5.anchor: فالوزر في الآية هو من: ضلال الحيرة وعدم الاهتداء إلى سواء السبيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r1.claim: God removed and nullified the Prophet's heavy burden completely and irreversibly; its weight made his back creak like a new saddle under a load.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r1.anchor: حططنا وأسقطنا وأبطلنا حطا لا رجعة له ولا فيه بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.claim: The burden was the strain of warning people by condemning their religion, ancestors, and judgment, which provoked their pride and threats of violence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r2.anchor: ما دهمه عندما أمر بإنذار قومه ومفاجأتهم بما يكرهون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r3.claim: God eased this strain through signs and forms of protection too extensive for anyone but Him to comprehend, as in the promise of protection from people.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r3.anchor: وضمن له من الحماية إلى أمور لا يحيط بها علما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r4.claim: Even worried relatives could not keep the Prophet from preaching: he pulled away and continued to tell people what they disliked, including around the Night Journey.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r4.anchor: فيجذب نفسه منه ويخرج إليهم فيخبرهم كما وقع في أمر الإسراء وغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the burden as Gabriel's opening the Prophet's chest, removing a dark clot, cleansing his heart, and filling it with knowledge, faith, and wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r5.anchor: هو أن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام شق صدره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r6.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās's account, the cleansing made the Prophet able to bear what others could not and made weighty matters easier for him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r6.anchor: يعني فصار يحتمل ما لا يحتمله غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r7.claim: Biqāʿī regards this as a valid lexical sense of burden; any interpretation as failure to fulfill an obligation is excluded because God protected the Prophet from it.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar b. al-Zubayr says al-Sharḥ continues al-Ḍuḥā's theme: both chapters enumerate God's favors to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r8.anchor: معنى هذه السورة من معنى السورة قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.claim: The chapters are separate because a benefactor first recounts favors that could seem earned, then original gifts granted before the recipient existed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r9.anchor: من المعهود في البشر فيمن عدد على ولده أو عبده نعما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.claim: The analogy is a parent first listing visible acts for a child, then the prior choice of the mother and provision made before the child's existence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p461/r10.anchor: أن يذكر له أولا ما شاهد الحصور عليه منها بسببه

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.claim: When the Prophet compared himself with earlier prophets' miracles, God reminded him of shelter, guidance, enrichment, an opened breast, removal of burden, and raised renown.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.claim: He says the Prophet's breast was filled with forbearance and knowledge, his burden was heavy, and his renown is raised whenever he is mentioned.
DURR-FULL:v8p547/r6.anchor: عن الحسن {ألم نشرح لك صدرك} قال: مليء حلما وعلما

DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.claim: He glosses the burden removed as the Prophet's sin and says it weighed heavily.
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} قال: ذنبك {الذي أنقض ظهرك} قال: أثقل

DURR-FULL:v8p548/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r3.speaker: شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r3.claim: He glosses the removal of the burden as forgiveness of the Prophet's sin.
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r3.anchor: عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي {ووضعنا عنك وزرك} قال: وغفرنا لك ذنبك

DURR-FULL:v8p548/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r4.claim: He records Abdullah's reading as ‘we removed your burden from you.’
DURR-FULL:v8p548/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: في قراءة عبد الله وحللنا عنك وقرك

NASHR:v1p218#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218#2/r1.claim: Rāʾ has an inherent repeated quality; pronounce a geminated rāʾ with one controlled rise, concealing its repetition without over-constriction or excessive thinning in light contexts.
NASHR:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: والراء: انفرد بكونه مكررا صفة لازمة له لغلظه. قال سيبويه: إذا تكلمت بها

NASHR:v1p218#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218#2/r2.claim: Make the voiced zāy in وزرك clear, especially when it is sākin and next to a voiceless consonant, so it does not approach sīn.
NASHR:v1p218#2/r2.anchor: والزاي: يتحفظ ببيان جهرها، لا سيما إذا سكنت نحو: تزدري،

NASHR:v1p218#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218#2/r3.claim: Keep sīn open and low after an emphatic consonant so it does not become ṣād; elsewhere preserve its whisper so it does not resemble zāy or jīm.
NASHR:v1p218#2/r3.anchor: والسين يعتنى ببيان انفتاحها واستفالها إذا أتى بعدها حرف إطباق

NASHR:v1p218#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218#2/r4.claim: Give shīn its distinctive spread, especially when geminated or sākin, and make it clearer in pause and in neighboring similar sounds.
NASHR:v1p218#2/r4.anchor: والشين: انفردت بصفة التفشي فليعن ببيانه، لا سيما في حال تشديدها، أو سكونها

NASHR:v1p218#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218#2/r5.claim: Keep ṣād distinct from sīn before tāʾ, from zāy before ṭāʾ, and from impermissible assimilation before dāl.
NASHR:v1p218#2/r5.anchor: والصاد: ليحترز حال سكونها إذا أتى بعدها تاء أن تقرب من السين نحو: ولو حرصت،

NASHR:v2p97/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p97/r1.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v2p97/r1.claim: Makkī and several authorities use emphatic rāʾ in وزرك and ذكرك to match the verse endings.
NASHR:v2p97/r1.anchor: وزرك، ذكرك. في ألم نشرح فخمها مكي، وصاحب التجريد، والمهدوي وابن سفيان

NASHR:v2p97/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p97/r2.speaker: الآخرون
NASHR:v2p97/r2.claim: Other authorities lighten the rāʾ in وزرك and ذكرك according to the regular rule.
NASHR:v2p97/r2.anchor: ورققها الآخرون على القياس. والوجهان في التذكرة والتلخيصين، والكافي.

NASHR:v2p97/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p97/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p97/r3.claim: Several works allow both forms and call emphatic rāʾ more common; al-Dānī read emphasis with Abū al-Fatḥ but chose the light reading.
NASHR:v2p97/r3.anchor: وقال: إن التفخيم فيهما أكثر. وحكى الوجهين في جامع البيان، وقال: إنه قرأ

ABUHAYYAN:94:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:94:2/r1.claim: Laying the burden aside is a metaphor for the Prophet's protection from sins and purification from impurities, stressing their complete absence.
ABUHAYYAN:94:2/r1.anchor: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس

ALUSI:94:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:2/r1.claim: The clause coordinates with the prior statement's implied sense: God expanded the Prophet's breast and removed his burden.
ALUSI:94:2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ } عطف على ما أشير إليه من مدلول الجملة السابقة

ALUSI:94:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:2/r2.claim: The prepositional phrase عنك precedes the direct object to hasten glad tidings and build anticipation for what comes later; postponing it would also disrupt the verse's cadence.
ALUSI:94:2/r2.anchor: وعنك متعلق بوضعنا وتقديمه على المفعول الصريح لما مر من القصد إلى تعجيل المسرة والتشويق إلى المؤخر

ALUSI:94:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:2/r3.claim: Wizr means a heavy load; the clause means God lifted the Prophet's heavy burden.
ALUSI:94:2/r3.anchor: والوزر الحمل الثقيل أي وحططنا عنك حملك الثقيل

BAGHAWI:94:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:2/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
BAGHAWI:94:2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say God removed what the Prophet had done in the pre-Islamic period, like the forgiveness mentioned at 48:2.
BAGHAWI:94:2/r1.anchor: قال الحسن ، وقتادة ، والضحاك : حططنا عنك الذي سلف منك في الجاهلية

BAGHAWI:94:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:2/r2.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
BAGHAWI:94:2/r2.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl interprets the burden as errors and forgetfulness.
BAGHAWI:94:2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل : يعني الخطأ والسهو

BAGHAWI:94:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:94:2/r3.claim: Another view says these are the community's sins, attributed to the Prophet because concern for them occupied his heart.
BAGHAWI:94:2/r3.anchor: وقيل : ذنوب أمتك فأضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بهم

BAYDAWI:94:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:2/r1.claim: The burden lifted from the Prophet is a heavy load.

BIQAI:94:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:2/r1.claim: Joining the removal of the burden to the preceding denial affirms it: a negative interrogative combined with negation becomes affirmation, allowing the conjunction.
BIQAI:94:2/r1.anchor: وكان الاستفهام الإنكاري إذا اجتمع مع النفي صار إثباتاً ،   لأنه نفي للنفي ،   قال عاطفاً عليه ما لا يعطف إلا مع الإثبات

BIQAI:94:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:2/r2.claim: Waḍaʿnā means God decisively lowered, removed, and annulled the burden, without return, by His might.
BIQAI:94:2/r2.anchor: أي حططنا وأسقطنا وأبطلنا حطاً لا رجعة له ولا فيه بوجه بما لنا من العظمة

BIQAI:94:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:2/r3.claim: Wizr is a heavy load that cannot be borne.
BIQAI:94:2/r3.anchor: أي حملك الثقيل الذي لا يستطاع حمله

BIQAI:94:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:2/r4.claim: Biqāʿī links this favor with the preceding expansion of the chest: knowledge and wisdom assemble virtues, while perfection also requires majesty through removing vices.
BIQAI:94:2/r4.anchor: ولما كانت سعة الصدر بالعلم والحكمة هي الجمال باجتماع المحاسن ،   وكان ذلك مع حمل ما يعني من أعظم النكد

DURR:94:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says the phrase about his back means it was heavy.
DURR:94:2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : ذنبك { الذي أنقض ظهرك } قال : أثقل

DURR:94:2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:2/r2.speaker: شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي
DURR:94:2/r2.claim: Shurayh ibn Ubayd glosses removing the burden as forgiving the Prophet's sin.
DURR:94:2/r2.anchor: عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : وغفرنا لك ذنبك

DURR:94:2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:2/r3.claim: Mujahid reports that Abdullah's reading has “and we relieved you of your burden.”
DURR:94:2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : في قراءة عبد الله «وحللنا عنك وقرك » .

DURR:94:3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says the phrase about his back means it was heavy.
