DURR:94:3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : ذنبك { الذي أنقض ظهرك } قال : أثقل

DURR:94:3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:3/r2.speaker: شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي
DURR:94:3/r2.claim: Shurayh ibn Ubayd glosses removing the burden as forgiving the Prophet's sin.
DURR:94:3/r2.anchor: عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } قال : وغفرنا لك ذنبك

DURR:94:3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:3/r3.claim: Mujahid reports that Abdullah's reading has “and we relieved you of your burden.”
DURR:94:3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : في قراءة عبد الله «وحللنا عنك وقرك » .

IBNASHUR:94:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:2/r1.claim: Wizr means distress or hardship; putting it down pictures removing trouble as lifting a weight from its bearer to relieve the strain.
IBNASHUR:94:2/r1.anchor: والوِزر :  الحَرج ،  ووضْعه :  حطَّه عن حامله ،  والكلام تمثيل لحال إزالة الشدائد والكروب

IBNASHUR:94:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:2/r2.claim: With revelation God freed the Prophet from the distress of pre-Islamic customs that clashed with his pure, elevated nature and that he had felt forced to accommodate.
IBNASHUR:94:2/r2.anchor: أن الله أزال عنه كل ما كان يتحرج منه من عادات أهل الجاهلية التي لا تلائم ما فطر الله عليه نفسه

IBNASHUR:94:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:2/r3.claim: God also eased the burden of early revelation by promising to make him recite without forgetting and to ease his path.
IBNASHUR:94:2/r3.anchor: وكذلك ما كان يجده في أول بعثته من ثقل الوحي فيسَّره الله عليه بقوله :  { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } إلى قوله

IBNASHUR:94:4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:4/r7.claim: Putting down the burden came through guidance that removed perplexity and provision that relieved the needs of living, as described at the end of al-Duha.
IBNASHUR:94:4/r7.anchor: وأما وضع الوزر عنه فحاصل بأمرين :  بهدايته إلى الحق التي أزالت حيرته بالتفكر في حال قومه

IBNASHUR:94:4/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:4/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:4/r13.claim: Although laka is not repeated with placing the burden, anka conveys both removal from him and personal care; its added emphasis also completes the syntax's general-then-specific expression.
IBNASHUR:94:4/r13.anchor: وإنما لم يذكر مع { ووضعنا عنك وزرك } بأن يقال :  ووضعنا لك وزرك للاستغناء بقوله :  { عنك }

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r1.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r1.claim: Some interpreters identify the burden as the Prophet's distress and confusion before his mission at seeing Quraysh worship idols, relieved by his prophethood and sending.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r1.anchor: و «الوزر » الذي وضعه الله عنه هو عند بعض المتأولين الثقل الذي كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وحيرته قبل المبعث إذ كان يرى سوء ما قريش فيه من عبادة الأصنام

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and others say God lightened the burdens of prophethood and helped the Prophet deal with people.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وغيره المعنى : خففنا عليك أثقال النبوة وأعناك على الناس

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r3.claim: The word originally means a weight; the majority of exegetes use it metaphorically for sins.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن زيد والحسن وجمهور من المفسرين : الوزر هنا ، الذنوب ، وأصله الثقل ، فشبهت الذنوب به

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r4.claim: The verse parallels the promise that God will forgive the Prophet's earlier and later sins.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية نظير قوله تعالى : { ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر }

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r5.claim: Before prophethood, the Prophet's burden included socializing with his people and eating their slaughtered animals and similar acts.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r5.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الجاهلية قبل النبوة وزره صحبة قومه وأكله من ذبائحهم ونحو هذا

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, as cited in al-Naqqāsh's book, says the burden included attending gatherings with his people that God disliked.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك : وفي كتاب النقاش حضوره مع قومه المشاهد التي لا يحبها الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r7.claim: Abū Muḥammad says these accounts fit together, including the Prophet's collecting arrows for his uncles at the Battle of al-Fijār; his heart remained inclined to right conduct and he never worshipped idols.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r7.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد : وهذه كلها ضمها المنشأ كشهوده حرب الفجار ينبل على أعمامه

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r8.claim: Anas ibn Mālik reads the phrase as wa-ḥaṭaṭnā ʿanka wizraka, using ḥaṭaṭnā for removing the burden.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك «وحططنا عنك وزرك »

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's codex has wa-ḥalalnā ʿanka wiqraka.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r9.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود «وحللنا عنك وقرك »

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r10.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r10.claim: Ubayy's codex instead has wa-ḥaṭaṭnā ʿanka wiqraka.

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr reports that the Prophet approved all these variant readings.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r11.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صوب جميعها

IBNATIYYA:94:2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r12.speaker: المحاسبي
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r12.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī says prophets' sins are called burdens because they are minor and forgiven, yet concern and remorse over them weigh on the prophets.
IBNATIYYA:94:2/r12.anchor: وقال المحاسبي : إنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء بالثقل ، وهي صغائر مغفورة لهمهم بها وتحسرهم عليها

IBNKATHIR:94:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:2/r1.claim: The removal of the Prophet's burden corresponds to God's promise to forgive his earlier and later sin in 48:2.
IBNKATHIR:94:2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ } بمعنى : { لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ }

MAWARDI:94:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:94:2/r1.claim: Waḍaʿnā ʿanka wizraka means God forgave the Prophet’s sin.
MAWARDI:94:2/r1.anchor: أحدها : وغفرنا لك ذنبك ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:94:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:94:2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins that weighed heavily on him, and God forgave them.
MAWARDI:94:2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة : كان للنبي ذنوب أثقلته فغفرها الله تعالى له

MAWARDI:94:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:94:2/r3.claim: The phrase means God lifted the Prophet’s burden; Ibn Masʿūd’s reading has the sense of loosening his load.
MAWARDI:94:2/r3.anchor: الثاني : وحططنا عنك ثقلك ، قاله السدي

MAWARDI:94:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:94:2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the phrase as wa-ḥalalnā ʿanka wiqraka, meaning God released the Prophet’s load.
MAWARDI:94:2/r4.anchor: وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود ، وحللنا عنك وقرك

MAWARDI:94:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:2/r5.claim: God kept the Prophet free of impurities during the forty years before prophethood, so revelation came to him while he was purified.
MAWARDI:94:2/r5.anchor: الثالث : وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس حتى نزل عليك الوحي وأنت مطهر

MAWARDI:94:2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:2/r6.claim: A further possibility is that God removed obligations beyond the Prophet’s capacity: prophets bear unusually heavy prophetic burdens but receive strength to carry them.
MAWARDI:94:2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل رابعاً : أي أسقطنا عنك تكليف ما لم تطقه ، لأن الأنبياء وإن حملوا من أثقال النبوة

NASAFI:94:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:2/r1.claim: God lightened the burdens of prophethood and carrying out its duties.
NASAFI:94:2/r1.anchor: وخففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها

NASAFI:94:2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:2/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:94:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the burden was an unspecified lapse: leaving the better while doing what is good; prophets may be reproached for this, and removing it means forgiving it.
NASAFI:94:2/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو زلة لا تعرف بعينها وهي ترك الأفضل مع إتيان الفاضل ، والأنبياء يعاتبون بمثلها

NASAFI:94:2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:2/r3.anchor: ووضعه عنه أن غفر له ، والوزر : الحمل الثقيل

QURTUBI:94:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:2/r1.claim: The phrase means that God lifted the Prophet's sin from him.
QURTUBI:94:2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ووضعنا عنك وزرك " أي حططنا عنك ذنبك

QURTUBI:94:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r2.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI:94:2/r2.claim: Anas is reported to read the phrase with the alternatives wa-ḥallalnā and wa-ḥaṭaṭnā.

QURTUBI:94:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:94:2/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads: We removed from you your burden.
QURTUBI:94:2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : " وحللنا عنك وقرك " .

QURTUBI:94:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:2/r4.claim: The verse parallels the forgiveness promised in 48:2.
QURTUBI:94:2/r4.anchor: هذه الآية مثل قوله تعالى : " ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

QURTUBI:94:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:2/r5.claim: One view places all of this before prophethood; al-Qurṭubī explains the burden as the Prophet's pre-Islamic ways shared with his people, although he never worshipped an idol or image.
QURTUBI:94:2/r5.anchor: قيل : الجميع كان قبل النبوة . والوزر : الذنب ، أي وضعنا عنك ما كنت فيه من أمر الجاهلية

QURTUBI:94:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.speaker: قتادة والحسن والضحاك
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the Prophet had sins weighing on him, which God forgave.
QURTUBI:94:2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة والحسن والضحاك : كانت للنبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ذنوب أثقلته ، فغفرها اللّه له

QURTUBI:94:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī says the burden would have weighed on him had God not pardoned him.
QURTUBI:94:2/r9.anchor: قال المحاسبي : يعني ثقل الوزر لو لم يعف اللّه عنه

QURTUBI:94:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains removing the burden as lifting the Prophet's weight.
QURTUBI:94:3/r3.anchor: وقال السدي : " ووضعنا عنك وزرك " أي وحططنا عنك ثقلك

QURTUBI:94:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd says: We lifted your burden from you.
QURTUBI:94:3/r4.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود " وحططنا عنك وقرك

QURTUBI:94:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.claim: Some explain the burden as the weight of pre-Islamic sins.
QURTUBI:94:3/r5.anchor: وقيل : أي حططنا عنك ثقل آثام الجاهلية

QURTUBI:94:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.speaker: الحسين بن المفضل
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mufaḍḍal takes it to mean error and inadvertence.
QURTUBI:94:3/r6.anchor: قال الحسين بن المفضل : يعني الخطأ والسهو

QURTUBI:94:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.claim: Some say the burden is the sins of the Prophet's community, attributed to him because his heart was occupied with them.
QURTUBI:94:3/r7.anchor: وقيل : ذنوب أمتك ، أضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها

QURTUBI:94:3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿUbayda say God lightened the burdens of prophethood and carrying it so it would not weigh on him.
QURTUBI:94:3/r8.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة : خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بها

QURTUBI:94:3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.claim: One account says revelation initially weighed on the Prophet until he nearly threw himself from a mountain; Gabriel showed himself and relieved his fear that his reason had changed.
QURTUBI:94:3/r9.anchor: وقيل : كان في الابتداء يثقل عليه الوحي ، حتى كاد يرمي نفسه من شاهق الجبل

QURTUBI:94:3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.claim: Another view says God protected him from bearing sin and kept him free of impurities through the forty years before revelation, which came to him purified.
QURTUBI:94:3/r10.anchor: وقيل : عصمناك عن احتمال الوزر ، وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس

RAZI:94:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:2/r1.speaker: المبرد
RAZI:94:2/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the clause coordinates with the meaning of “Did We not expand,” understood as “We have expanded,” rather than its surface wording; literal coordination would require “and We will remove.”
RAZI:94:2/r1.anchor: قال المبرد : هذا محمول على معنى ألم نشرح

RAZI:94:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:94:2/r2.claim: Wizr means the weight of sin; Rāzī links the phrase to 6:31, where people carry their burdens, and to the forgiveness promised in 48:2.

TAB:94:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:94:2/r1.claim: The opening reminds the Prophet of God's favors and kindness to prompt gratitude and make him worthy of further blessing.
TAB:94:2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ذكره لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   مذكّره آلاءه عنده ،   وإحسانه إليه ،   حاضا له بذلك على شكره

TAB:94:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r3.speaker: author
TAB:94:2/r3.claim: God removed the burden by forgiving past sins and lifting the weight of the Prophet's days in the Jāhiliyya.
TAB:94:2/r3.anchor: وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ يقول :  وغفرنا لك ما سلف من ذنوبك ،   وحططنا عنك ثقل أيام الجاهلية التي كنت فيها

TAB:94:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB:94:2/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has “wa-ḥalalnā ʿanka wiqraka” in place of “wa-waḍaʿnā ʿanka wizraka.”
TAB:94:2/r4.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر :  «وَحَلَلْنا عَنْكَ وِقْرَكَ » الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ يقول

TAB:94:2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:2/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the burden as the Prophet's sin and says it weighed heavily on his back.
TAB:94:2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  ذنبك .   وقوله :  أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ قال :  أثقل ظهرك

TAB:94:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB:94:2/r7.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins that weighed him down, which God forgave.
TAB:94:2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمَ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ :  كانت للنبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

TAB:94:2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:94:2/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the burden as the shirk the Prophet had been in.
TAB:94:2/r8.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول ،   في قوله :  وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ يعني :  الشرك الذي كان فيه .

TAB:94:2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says God expanded the Prophet's chest and forgave the sin he had before being commissioned as a prophet.
TAB:94:2/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ألَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ قال :  شرح له صدرَه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p91/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p91/r1.claim: Wizrak means your sin: the original sense of wizr is a load carried on the back, so sin is metaphorically treated as a burden; 20:87 and 29:13 use loads for sins.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p91/r1.anchor: أي إثمك. وأصل الوزر: ما حمله الإنسان على ظهره. قال الله عز وجل: ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم

ITQAN:v1p127/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p127/r1.claim: In a report from Ibn Umar in Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet says revelation comes with ringing sounds and leaves him silent; when it arrives, he fears his soul may be taken.
ITQAN:v1p127/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هل تحس بالوحي فقال أسمع صلاصل ثم أسكت عند ذلك فما من مرة يوحي إلي

ITQAN:v1p127/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r2.speaker: الخطابي
ITQAN:v1p127/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi explains that the sound is continuous and not clear at first; its meaning becomes understood afterward.
ITQAN:v1p127/r2.anchor: قال الخطابي والمراد أنه صوت متدارك يسمعه ولا يبين له أول ما يسمعه حتى يفهمه بعد

ITQAN:v1p127/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p127/r3.claim: An alternative says the sound is the fluttering of the angel's wings.
ITQAN:v1p127/r3.anchor: وقيل هو صوت خفق أجنحة الملك

ITQAN:v1p127/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p127/r4.claim: The advance sound clears the Prophet's hearing for revelation so nothing else occupies it.
ITQAN:v1p127/r4.anchor: والحكمة في تقدمه أن يفرغ سمعه للوحي فلا يبقي فيه مكانا لغيره

ITQAN:v1p127/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p127/r5.claim: The sound-like mode is described in the Sahih as the most severe state of revelation for the Prophet.
ITQAN:v1p127/r5.anchor: وفي الصحيح أن هذه الحالة أشد حالات الوحي عليه

ITQAN:v1p127/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r6.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p127/r6.claim: Some say revelation came in this form when a verse of warning or threat was sent down.
ITQAN:v1p127/r6.anchor: وقيل إنه إنما كان ينزل هكذا إذا نزلت آية وعيد وتهديد

ITQAN:v1p127/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p127/r7.claim: A report cited by al-Hakim says the Holy Spirit breathed the words into the Prophet's heart.
ITQAN:v1p127/r7.anchor: الثانية أن ينفث في روعه الكلام نفثا كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن روح القدس نفث في روعي أخرجه الحاكم

ITQAN:v1p127/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p127/r8.claim: The inward breathing may accompany either the sound-like mode or the angel's appearance in human form.
ITQAN:v1p127/r8.anchor: وهذا قد يرجع إلى الحالة الأولى أو التي بعدها بأن يأتيه في إحدى الكيفيتين وينفث في روعه

ITQAN:v1p127/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p127/r9.claim: In a Sahih report, the Prophet says the angel sometimes appears as a man, speaks to him, and he understands the words.
ITQAN:v1p127/r9.anchor: الثالثة أن يأتيه في صورة الرجل فيكلمه كما في الصحيح وأحيانا يتمثل لي الملك رجلا فيكلمني فأعي ما يقول

ITQAN:v1p127/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r10.speaker: أبو عوانة
ITQAN:v1p127/r10.claim: Abu Awana's version adds that the angel's appearance as a man was the easiest form for the Prophet.
ITQAN:v1p127/r10.anchor: زاد أبو عوانة في صحيحه وهو أهونه علي

ITQAN:v1p127/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p127/r11.claim: A further mode is that the angel comes to the Prophet in sleep.
ITQAN:v1p127/r11.anchor: الرابعة أن يأتيه الملك في النوم وعد من هذا قوم سورة الكوثر

ITQAN:v1p127/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r12.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v1p127/r12.claim: Some classify the revelation of Surat al-Kawthar as an instance of the angel's coming during sleep.
ITQAN:v1p127/r12.anchor: وعد من هذا قوم سورة الكوثر وقد تقدم ما فيه

ITQAN:v1p127/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p127/r13.claim: A report of Muadh describes God speaking to the Prophet in a dream, asking what the exalted assembly dispute about; the source also names God's speech to him while awake on the Night Journey.
ITQAN:v1p127/r13.anchor: الخامسة أن يكلمه الله إما في اليقظة كما في ليلة الإسراء أو في النوم كما في حديث معاذ أتاني ربي فقال فيم يختصم الملأ الأعلى

ITQAN:v1p127/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p127/r14.claim: The author says he knows no Qur'anic instance of this mode, though the end of al-Baqara and portions of al-Duha and al-Sharh may count as exceptions.
ITQAN:v1p127/r14.anchor: وليس في القرآن من هذا النوع شيء فيما أعلم نعم يمكن أن يعد منه آخر سورة البقرة لما تقدم وبعض سورة الضحى وألم نشرح

ITQAN:v1p127/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p127/r15.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p127/r15.claim: Adi ibn Thabit reports the Prophet's account of a divine response: God recalls sheltering him as an orphan, guiding and enriching him, expanding his breast, removing his burden, and raising his mention, and says He is mentioned whenever the Prophet is.
ITQAN:v1p127/r15.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم من حديث عدي بن ثابت قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أكن سألته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r1.claim: Waḍʿ means putting something down or leaving it, usually by lowering it from above to below.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r1.anchor: الوضع : إلقاء الشيء وتركه . والغالب فيه أن يكون إلقاؤه من العلو إلى السفل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r2.claim: Waḍīʿ describes someone low in lineage or social standing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r2.anchor: والوضيع : الدني في حسبه ضعة وضعة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r3.claim: For a riding animal, waḍʿ is a smooth, quick gait; a rider can make it move at that pace.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r3.anchor: والدابة تضع في سيرها وضعا وهو سير سهل سريع . وأوضعها راكبها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r4.claim: One Qur'anic sense is giving birth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r4.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الوضع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r5.claim: A second sense is lowering or removing a burden; this is the sense in the target verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الوضع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r6.claim: A third sense is setting something in place, as with the balances and the record on Judgment Day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الوضع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r7.claim: A fourth sense is spreading or laying out the earth for creatures.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الوضع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r8.claim: A fifth sense is marching or moving swiftly through a group.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الوضع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r9.speaker: اليزيدي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r9.claim: Al-Yazidi glosses īḍāʿ as quick travel; in the verse it means they would hurry along among the people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p611/r9.anchor: قال اليزيدي : الإيضاع : سرعة السير . ومعناه لأسرعوا السير بينكم يتخللونكم

DAMGHANI:v1p490/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r2.claim: Waḍaʿnā means we removed or lifted away a burden.
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r2.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك أي حططنا عنك

BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking about gifts given to other men; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him. Other transmitters add that God expanded his breast and removed his burden.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته
